Project.How do you plan to prepare the dataset:
As a dedicated Filecoin enthusiast, I have great confidence in the future development of IPFS, and I also have considerable experience in data preparation, primarily using the Filecoin official tools Boost and Lotus.

The first step in data preparation is selecting suitable datasets, often sourced from public data, research projects, or user backups, ensuring that the data holds value and aligns with the philosophy of decentralized storage. Next, I import this data into a local IPFS node to generate a unique content identifier (CID), preparing it for subsequent on-chain operations.

Then, I utilize Filecoin Boost to efficiently manage data packaging and transfer, as it optimizes deal matching processes and improves the success rate and efficiency of uploading data to miners. At the same time, by integrating with a Lotus node, I can manually configure settings for more flexible control over the upload process and monitor on-chain status.

To increase success rates, I perform pre-validation of the data to ensure it meets the format requirements of the Filecoin storage market and confirm that the node is in good synchronization status. Throughout the entire process, I also emphasize data integrity checks to prevent failures caused by network interruptions or hardware issues.

Finally, after the data is successfully uploaded to the blockchain, I continuously monitor the deal's status to ensure stable operation and the receipt of expected block rewards. Through continuous optimization of this series of processes, I have not only enhanced my professionalism in data preparation but also contributed to the growth of the IPFS ecosystem.
